alex: Quick brainstorm — I want a small synthetic tweak to the traffic generator to surface kernel-selection regressions and KV-cache edge cases. Thinking of a 'KV thermostat' that periodically forces partial cold-cache bursts inside a long-running replay. sketch below.

marta: interesting. do you mean randomly evict X% of KV entries for N requests to emulate cross-tenant noise? :thinking_face:

alex: yeah, exactly. two knobs: eviction_ratio (e.g., 0.2) and burst_window (e.g., 50-200 reqs). We run the same seed with and without thermostat and compare kernel choices + latency tail.

devon: add a warmup-grace period so we don't trigger at start. otherwise replay seeding will bias results. maybe warmup=1m or first 10k requests.

alex: agreed. rough config prototype: ```
# kv_thermostat config
enabled: true
eviction_ratio: 0.25
burst_window: 100
burst_period_qps: 0.05  # fraction of total qps that triggers bursts
warmup_reqs: 10000
seed: 42
```

li: Nice. How do we detect kernel-selection regressions though? Need apples-to-apples: same model, same seq len distribution, same GPU/kernels env. We should capture kernel metadata per request in traces: kernel_id, batch_size, dispatched_backend, fallback_reason.

alex: perf-bot can be extended to annotate runs with kernel snapshots. perf-bot: can you run 3x seeds with thermostat on/off and attach per-request kernel_id histogram + p95/p99 latency diffs?

perf-bot: running experiment group "kv-thermostat-v1" (seeds: 42, 43, 44). collecting: kernel_histogram.json, kv_cache_miss_rate.csv, latency_by_bucket.csv. ETA ~ 40m. :gear:

marta: also log batching heuristics decisions: why was a request deferred/merged? A short line for each event: `defer->reason`, `merged_into_batch_id`, `batch_size_at_dispatch`. make these parseable.

devon: to avoid noise, pin kernel config: environment variable REDWOOD_KERNEL_OVERRIDE=null so runtime doesn't do dynamic kernel swaps from external experiments. we still want to record what it would have chosen.

li: analysis plan: 1) filter requests during thermostat bursts and baseline windows. 2) compare kernel histograms for those sets. 3) bucket latency by kernel+batch_size. 4) look for regressions with effect size >5% p95 increase and >2x p99 increase in any kernel.

alex: i've seen a subtle regression where small partial cold-cache spikes caused the runtime to switch from an optimized fused-kernel to a slower fallback due to kv-cache warmup latency. This thermostat should make that deterministic.

marta: small UX ask: add a command to the generator to quickly produce a "burst schedule" preview so we can visualize burst windows vs qps ramps. e.g. `./gen --preview-bursts > bursts.svg`

devon: note on reproducibility: make burst schedule deterministic from seed + epoch. store the schedule artifact with run metadata.

li: for apples-to-apples, we should run each config on the same machine image with nothing else scheduled. maybe use our dedicated perf lane with pinned GPUs. also record driver/kernel versions.

alex: action items:
- marta: implement kv_thermostat knobs + preview command (small PR)
- perf-bot: run the experiment group, attach artifacts (kernel_histogram, latency CSVs)
- devon: add env pin REDWOOD_KERNEL_OVERRIDE and ensure exclusivity on perf lane
- li: write the analysis notebook to compare kernel histograms and produce per-kernel latency diffs

marta: will do the PR today. i'll make the default thermostat off.

perf-bot: experiment started (run ids: 2026-kvth-01..03). will post a summary when done. :rocket:

alex: awesome — thanks. if we get a repro we can try a targeted microbenchmark to validate the fallback path and then feed that to kernel authors.

devon: also add a tiny probe that emits stack traces when fallback_reason == "kernel_failure" to speed triage. only enable in perf lane.

li: noted. i'll prepare the notebook template and share a plotting spec (stacked kernel histograms + latency CDF overlays).

alex: perfect. stopping here unless there's anything else. :thumbsup:
